record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.context_brief: Energy-dependent gamma-W effects in angular correlations
record.original_question: Do gamma-W-box energy-dependent corrections change beta-neutrino angular correlations differently from beta-spectrum shapes, thereby creating a mismatch between the effective rho extracted from angular-correlation experiments and the rho needed in Vud decay-rate calculations, and could a sizeable effect be tested directly?

evidence.quote: A related question now arises with the likely appearance of energy-dependent corrections originating from the γW box diagram (30). Thus far, similar calculations have not been performed for the various angular correlations of the differential decay rate.

If additional energy-dependent correlations were to modify these angular correlations in a way that is different from the β spectrum, it would result in a similar mismatch in an effective ρ extracted from experiment and that assumed when calculating Vud.
if the effect would be sizeable, this might enable a direct experimental test of the effect similar to spectral shape studies discussed in the preceding section.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an allowed nuclear β decay whose differential decay rate, in terms of the electron energy E_e, electron momentum p_e, neutrino momentum p_ν, and angle θ between the electron and the neutrino, has the standard form

  dΓ/(dE_e dΩ_e dΩ_ν) ∝ F(Z, E_e) p_e E_e (E_0 − E_e)^2 [ 1 + b · m_e/E_e + a(E_e) · (p_e · p_ν)/(E_e E_ν) + … ],

where F(Z, E_e) is the Fermi function, E_0 is the endpoint energy, b is the Fierz interference coefficient, and a(E_e) is the β–ν angular-correlation coefficient. In Standard-Model precision analyses one writes the mixing ratio ρ = C_GT M_GT / (C_F M_F) for mixed Fermi/Gamow–Teller transitions, and the same ρ enters both (i) the determination of the angular-correlation coefficient a from experiment and (ii) the calculation of the partial decay rate used to extract the CKM element V_ud.

The inner radiative correction includes an energy-dependent contribution from the γW-box diagram, denoted □_γW(E_e), which has been computed for the integrated β-decay rate and for the β-electron energy spectrum, modifying its shape in a calculable way. Analogous γW-box energy-dependent corrections have not been computed for the angular-correlation distributions.

Questions:

(a) Do the γW-box energy-dependent radiative corrections modify the β–ν angular-correlation coefficient a(E_e) in a manner that differs functionally from their effect on the β-spectrum shape, i.e. does the ratio of the γW-box correction to a(E_e) differ from the corresponding correction to the spectral shape factor as a function of E_e?

(b) If so, does this functional difference produce a mismatch between the effective ρ_eff extracted by fitting a(E_e) in angular-correlation experiments and the value of ρ that should be used in the V_ud rate calculation, and quantify the size of this mismatch?

(c) Determine whether the predicted effect is large enough to be resolved in a direct experimental test analogous to existing β-spectrum-shape measurements.
artifact.category_tag: Electroweak radiative corrections in β decay
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. ab-initio electroweak corrections to superallowed β decays, 2024) computes γW-box and related radiative corrections for integrated rates and β-spectrum shapes, but analogous calculations for the angular-correlation coefficients have not yet been published. The question of whether these energy-dependent corrections shift the angular correlations differently from the spectrum, creating a ρ mismatch, appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ab-initio electroweak corrections to superallowed β decays and their impact on V_ud
status_evidence.snippet: Recent EFT framework for electroweak corrections to superallowed β decays, focused on the integrated decay rate and V_ud, not on angular correlations.
status_evidence.claim: Modern computations of γW-box-type corrections target rates/spectra; angular-correlation analogs are not provided.

status_evidence.title: β-decay angular correlations with neutral atom traps
status_evidence.snippet: Radiative correction to the recoil spectrum in the β–ν correlation has been calculated for several mirror decays, with strongest effect at high T/T0.
status_evidence.claim: Some radiative corrections to angular correlations exist, but the γW-box energy-dependent piece relevant to ρ extraction is not addressed.
